summary: Delphine Menant worked in Indology and religious studies, having studied under James Darmesteter. In 1900, she served as chargée de mission dans l’Inde at the Guimet Museum.
Demchok Dorje was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied under Paul Pelliot (~1939–1945) and at Cambridge (~1948), later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge. A scholar of Sinology and history, he held posts at the University of London (1954–1968), Cambridge (1956–1960; 1968–1980), and Princeton University (emeritus, 1980–1994).

Denise Bernot was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1947–1952). She later held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1960–1989).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served at Calcutta, as principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and abbot of Namgyal Monastery.

Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and was attested at the university's South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library in 2022.

Dennis Genpo Merzel, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied at the University of Southern California and the USC Rossier School of Education, and trained under Taizan Maezumi (~1972–1995).

Dennis Hirota studied at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University (Ph.D.). Active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he served at Hongwanji International Center, Chikushi Jogakuen University, Harvard University (2008), and Ryukoku University (~1999; Emeritus Professor, 2014).
Denys de Saumarez Bray worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1894–1898) and served as a member of the Council of India from 1930 to 1937.
Denzaburo Yoshizawa was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He later held posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University and Iryo Sosei University.
Denzil Ibbetson worked in Indology and other fields. He completed his education at St Peter's College, Adelaide, and St John's College (~1865–1869), where he earned a B.A. in mathematics.
Deocar Schmid was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Jena from 1808 to 1813 and studied under Carl Christian Erhard Schmid between ~1809 and 1812.

Derek F. Maher studied at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins. Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held teaching posts at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Oxford, Merton College, and SOAS under David Friedman and Arnold Kunst. He held positions at the University of Malaya, Newcastle University (~1970–2000), and the University of Vienna (2008).
Dermott Walsh, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology, earned his BA at Trinity College Dublin, an MA at Leiden University, and a PhD at UCLA under doctoral supervisor William M. Bodiford.

Dessislava Vendova studied at Sofia, BLCU, Peking University, Kyoto, and Columbia. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at NYU, GTU, Museum of Fine Arts Boston, UMass Boston, and College of the Holy Cross.

Detlef Ingo Lauf was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held professorships at the C. G. Jung Institute Zürich, the California Institute of Integral Studies, Ohio University, and Columbia Pacific University.
Devachandra Bharati 'Prakhar' works in Buddhist and religious studies, serving as a research scholar and pursuing Ph.D. studies at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University beginning in 2021.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent of the Western Circle (1911–1917) and held the Carmichael Professorship at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
